'''Kern River Gas Pipeline''' is a proposed natural gas pipeline.<ref name=source1>[http://bit.ly/2crGH1S Kern River Gas Pipeline,] Wikipedia, accessed September 2017</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs from Opal, Wyoming through Utah and Nevada to Daggett, California.

==Background==
The Kern River Gas Pipeline is owned and operated by Berkshire Hathaway Energy.<ref>[https://www.berkshirehathawayenergyco.com/news/midamerican-energy-holdings-company-is-now-berkshire-hathaway-energy Kern River Gas Transmission Company - About Us], Berkshire Hathaway Energy, accessed January 2018</ref>

In 2003, a system expansion added 716 miles (1,152.3 kilometers) and 900 million cubic feet per day of transport capacity. The pipeline has a diameter of 36-inches and cost US$1.3 billion to complete.<ref name=eia>[https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php Natural Gas Data, Pipeline Projects] Energy Information Agency, accessed July 21, 2020</ref>

==Environmental Impact==
A 1992 report by the U.S. Geological Survey documented the potential for the Kern River Gas Pipeline and other pipelines to damage the environment in the Mojave Desert. "Residual environmental effects of the pipeline installations described above include
accelerated wind and water erosion and long-term loss of habitat. Accelerated wind erosion has resulted in property damage, public safety hazards, possibly deleterious health effects on humans and domestic and wild animals, and enlargement of damage to plant communities adjacent to construction corridors.<ref>[https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1992/0447/report.pdf Wilshire, H.G., 1992, Environmental impacts of pipeline corridors in the Mojave Desert, California, p.9], U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 92-477, 1992</ref>

* '''Operator:''' Kern River Gas Transmission Company<ref name=":0" />
*'''Owner:''' Kern River Gas Transmission Company<ref name=":0" />
*'''Parent company:''' Berkshire Hathaway<ref name=":0" />
* '''Capacity:''' 140,000 Dth/d (dekatherms per day)<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ferc.gov/media/c-1-cp21-197-000|title=C-1-CP21-197-000 {{!}} Federal Energy Regulatory Commission|website=www.ferc.gov|language=en|access-date=2022-05-20}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php|title=Natural Gas Data - U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)|website=www.eia.gov|access-date=2023-08-08}}</ref>
* '''Length:''' 35.84 miles<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=https://www.kernrivergas.com/DesktopModules/KernRiver/Documents/ViewDocument.aspx?DocumentID=59|title=Delta Lateral Project fact sheet|last=|first=|date=|website=Kern River Gas|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=08 August 2023}}</ref>
* '''Diameter:''' 24 inches<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" />
* '''Status:''' Operating<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://www.kernrivergas.com/Projects/Delta-Lateral-Project|title=https://www.kernrivergas.com/Projects/Delta-Lateral-Project|url-status=live}}</ref>
* '''Start year:''' 2024<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":6" />
* '''Cost:''' US$93,140,275<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4" />
* '''Financing:'''
* '''Associated infrastructure:'''


The Delta Lateral would carry natural gas from Kern River's mainline hear Holden, Utah to a delivery point near Delta, Utah, United States.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.kernrivergas.com/DesktopModules/KernRiver/Documents/ViewDocument.aspx?DocumentID=59|title=Delta Lateral Project|last=|first=|date=|website=Kern River Gas|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2022-05-20}}</ref> The project is expected deliver natural gas to Intermountain Power Agency's Intermountain Power Project.<ref name=":4" />

The project was first proposed in Spring 2020, and FERC approved Kern River's pre-filing process in July 2020.<ref name=":2" />

On 19 May 2022, FERC issued a certificate approving the project. Construction was expected to begin during Spring 2023, and it was slated to go into service during Spring 2024.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />

The pipeline was placed in service on 1 April 2024.<ref name=":6" />
